Anthropic Hiring Manager Declares End of Traditional Coding Interviews, Citing AI Superiority

01 Nov 2026, 06:34 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.techradar.com

Overview

An engineering manager at Anthropic, identified as Felix Rieseberg, announced that he has stopped using conventional coding interviews because the company's AI system, Claude, can perform coding tasks more effectively than human candidates.

Rationale

In a blog post, Rieseberg explained that "this month, I laid the traditional coding interview to rest." He argues that coding challenges are no longer meaningful when an AI can write, debug, and optimise code better than a person, stating that "there’s no more point in giving you a little React challenge than there is in quizzing people about assembly; Claude is now better at both."

Shift in Hiring Approach

Rieseberg encourages junior engineers to focus on making an impact and understanding the company and its people rather than demonstrating raw coding speed. He suggests evaluating candidates by looking for prototypes that show "taste, empathy, and principled thinking," and by reviewing portfolios that include AI‑augmented projects.

Practical Implications

  • Interview redesign: Companies may need to replace algorithmic puzzles with assessments of real‑world project outcomes, especially those that leverage AI tools.
  • Candidate preparation: Prospective hires should showcase AI‑enhanced prototypes and the ability to integrate them thoughtfully into products, rather than solely emphasizing coding speed.
  • Team culture: Emphasising "hunger beats tenure" signals a shift toward valuing drive and impact over seniority in a landscape where AI can automate many routine tasks.

How to Verify the Announcement

To confirm Rieseberg’s statements, readers can:

  • Locate his original blog post on Anthropic’s website or the linked TechRadar article.
  • Review any public statements or press releases from Anthropic that reference changes to their hiring process.
  • Check for follow‑up coverage in reputable tech news outlets that quote Rieseberg directly.

Unknowns / Open Questions

  • The specific criteria Anthropic will use to assess "taste, empathy, and principled thinking" remain undefined in the source.
  • It is unclear whether other AI‑focused organisations will adopt similar interview reforms.
  • The practical meaning of "hunger beats tenure" in day‑to‑day performance evaluation has not been elaborated.

While Rieseberg’s decision reflects a broader industry trend toward AI‑augmented workflows, the full impact on hiring practices and candidate evaluation methods is still emerging.
